summary: Converts rows into columns and columns into rows, swapping a table's orientation for downstream lookup, export, or reshaping workflows.

key_params.name: input0
key_params.note: Source table whose rows and columns are swapped

key_params.name: wordwrap
key_params.note: Common DAT node display wrapping setting

key_params.name: customext
key_params.note: Custom editor extension when extension mode uses a custom extension

common_gotchas: The first input row becomes the first output column, so header rows become header columns.
Downstream DAT references by row or column index may need to be rewritten after transposing.
Empty cells remain empty but their coordinates change with the table orientation.
Transpose DAT has no operator-specific page parameters, so use upstream DATs for filtering or renaming.
For one-row key/value tables, verify whether downstream consumers expect keys across columns or down rows.
key_concepts: Transpose DAT swaps input table rows and columns.
The output row count becomes the input column count and the output column count becomes the input row count.
It operates on its input table directly and exposes only common DAT controls.
Info CHOP channels report common DAT dimensions such as num_rows and num_cols after transposition.
